identity.name: Nukleus Office Solutions Limited
identity.industry: Flexible workspace / managed office & co-working operator (commercial real-estate services, asset-light lease/sub-lease model)

summary.oneLiner: Nukleus is a small (~Rs 36 cr revenue), profitable, asset-light flexible-workspace operator (co-working + managed office) concentrated in Delhi NCR with a recent Bengaluru entry, executing a strategic pivot from co-working toward higher-growth managed-office/back-to-back deals and guiding to ~10 lakh sq ft operational area by end-FY27 (up from ~3.5 lakh sq ft today) — a claimed ~10x area expansion since its SME IPO, though management explicitly declined to quantify the revenue this will translate into, and mid-call, management flagged and could not resolve an internal inconsistency in its own segment-revenue-mix slide.

one-line thesis: Nukleus is a small (~Rs 36 cr revenue), profitable, asset-light flexible-workspace operator (co-working + managed office) concentrated in Delhi NCR with a recent Bengaluru entry, executing a strategic pivot from co-working toward higher-growth managed-office/back-to-back deals and guiding to ~10 lakh sq ft operational area by end-FY27 (up from ~3.5 lakh sq ft today) — a claimed ~10x area expansion since its SME IPO, though management explicitly declined to quantify the revenue this will translate into, and mid-call, management flagged and could not resolve an internal inconsistency in its own segment-revenue-mix slide.
financial scorecard (track qoq/yoy):
| Metric | FY26 | YoY | Note |
|---|---|---|---|
| Total income (FY26) | Rs 36.19 cr | +25.49% (MD) / +23.6% (CEO, same call) | Two different YoY growth figures given by two speakers for the same FY26 total-income number — flagged, not reconciled on the call |
| Total income (H2 FY26) | Rs 18.88 cr (1,888.35 lakh) | +30.12% YoY | |
| EBITDA (FY26) | Rs 9.17 cr (917.34 lakh) | +38.12% (MD) / +38.10% (CEO) | Consistent across speakers |
| EBITDA (H2 FY26) | Rs 5.08 cr (507.85 lakh) | +35.16% YoY | |
| PAT (FY26) | Rs 2.14 cr (213.53 lakh) | not stated numerically (3-yr trend chart referenced: "from 1 to 2.13" implying prior-year PAT ~Rs 1 cr) | |
| Fixed assets | Rs 35.25 cr (3,525.36 lakh) | +160.71% YoY | Driven by workspace infra/tech-platform/managed-office expansion capex |
| Net worth (FY26-end) | Rs 41 cr | — | |
| Total liabilities / current liabilities | Rs 24 cr / Rs 11 cr | — | |
| Total assets (equity+liabilities) | Rs 76.64 cr (non-current Rs 53 cr + current Rs 22 cr ≈ Rs 76 cr) | — | Minor rounding gap between the two totals as read out |
| Cash & bank balance | Rs 7.56 cr | — | |
| Finance cost | stated as "~11.5 lakh vs 92.75 lakh, +~8%" | — | Numbers as read out are internally inconsistent (11.5 < 92.75 cannot be a +8% increase) — likely a transcription/verbal slip for ~Rs 115 lakh vs Rs 92.75 lakh (~+24%); flagged, not company-confirmed |
> **One-offs / data-quality flags (call them out explicitly):** (1) Management itself flagged an error live on the call in the revenue-by-segment (co-working vs managed office) pie-chart slide — CEO Ajay Singhal said managed-office FY25 base of "961"/"951" was showing lower at "783" and asked participants to disregard the chart pending correction; CBO Abhimanyu Singh confirmed they will "correct the numbers... in the next edition." Segment-mix % given verbally instead (see §5). (2) The finance-cost figures as read out are numerically inconsistent (see table) — treat with caution until re-confirmed. (3) Company plans to convert to Ind-AS ("Ind AS" — mis-transcribed as "index"/"NDS" in places) only "this financial year" (FY27), i.e. FY26 numbers above are pre-Ind-AS, not yet lease-accounting (right-of-use) adjusted — flagged by an analyst as a potential margin-comparability issue vs listed larger peers who report on Ind-AS/IFRS.
guidance (critical — verify next quarter:
- Revenue growth: No explicit revenue number given for FY27; management explicitly declined to quantify ("putting a number to this is something I don't think is a good idea at this kind of stage").
- Area/portfolio: current ~7+ lakh sq ft signed/committed (~3.5 lakh sq ft operational); guiding to "more than a million [10 lakh] sq ft operational" by end of FY27 — described as ~10x growth in operational area since IPO (IPO base ~1.0–1.15 lakh sq ft per RHP). Management cautioned the full 10 lakh sq ft will not all contribute to FY27 revenue — benefit flows through FY27 and into FY28 given a stated 3-month centre-setup cycle plus a further 3–6 month occupancy-stabilization period per new centre.
- Segment mix target: co-working:managed-office was ~70:30 at IPO, currently ~50:50; guided to ~70:30 in favour of managed office over the next 3–4 years, eventually ~90:10 managed-office:co-working long-term.
- Margin: no explicit consolidated margin guidance; qualitative order given (illustrative, "not in real terms" per CBO): co-working ~30% profit %, managed office ~25%, back-to-back deals ~20% — i.e. margin decreases as the company scales toward the higher-growth managed/back-to-back segments.
- Capex / accounting: Ind-AS conversion targeted "this financial year" (FY27) per MD. GCC: first GCC client enrolment expected "very, very soon"; company is participating in GCC RFPs. New city expansion into Pune and Hyderabad "over this financial year," in addition to existing Delhi NCR and Bengaluru presence.
- 5-year vision (qualitative, unquantified): sustain the current pace of sq-ft addition (not the same growth %, similar absolute increment) for the next five years; ambition to be a national-brand operator across India's top-5 office markets and "one of the biggest" operators within three years.
order book & pipeline: No formal "order book" metric disclosed (real-estate leasing business, not manufacturing/EPC). Pipeline proxy: ~7+ lakh sq ft signed and under various stages of fit-out/utilization (vs. ~3.5 lakh sq ft currently operational); named upcoming projects: Wave One and Shivaji Stadium Metro Station (Noida/Delhi NCR). Managed-office contract tenures cited at 4–9 years, providing revenue visibility once operational (no vacancy gap on back-to-back deals per management).
segment / subsidiary detail:
- Portfolio: 25 centres total — 17 co-working + 8 managed-office centres, ~85% occupancy, present across 4 cities (Delhi NCR the dominant base — flagship centres Noida Sector-142/Logix Cyber Park, Skymark, Okaya, NSL IFCO Tower Gurgaon; Barakhamba Tower, Thapar House, Pegasus in Delhi; entry into Bengaluru via Prestige Blue Chip, Dairy Circle CBD).
- Segment mix (verbal, since the slide/chart was flagged as erroneous): co-working ~50%, managed office ~50% currently (from ~70:30 co-working-heavy at IPO); managed-office growing ~30–40%/yr vs co-working ~10%/yr.
- No subsidiaries — standalone entity; two executive directors on board (Nipun Gupta – MD; Pooja Gupta – Executive Director, finance) plus independent directors Ajay Kumar and P N Sharma.
growth verticals / optionality: GCC (Global Capability Centre) demand — company positioning itself for enterprise/GCC-grade requirements (data-centre tie-ups, HR/travel infra, real-estate "added services"); first GCC client onboarding expected imminently. Technology stack (AI voice assistant for lead/call handling, client mobile app, smart inventory management, EIS/CRM dashboards) cited as driver of sales-conversion and turnaround-time efficiency gains, indirectly supporting margin expansion.
6a. moat & competitive position (optiona:
- Strong NCR micro-market presence across most sub-markets with "marquee" assets (evidenced by named flagship centres and inventory concentration in Noida Sector-142 — ~1.5–2 lakh sq ft in that one sector alone).
- Shift toward landlord-funded fit-outs / revenue-sharing deals (rather than company capex on fit-outs) as brand recognition improves — reduces future capital intensity, per management.
- Management explicitly conceded the industry is nascent/fragmented ("even the biggest player has only 2% of the inventory," "nobody is big") — i.e. no claimed scale moat versus larger organised peers; competitive position rests on execution/tech rather than durable structural barriers.
margins & cost dynamics: EBITDA margin expansion (FY26 EBITDA +38% YoY vs revenue +23.6–25.5% YoY) attributed by management primarily to operating leverage/productivity gains from technology (AI-assisted call filtering cut agent call-handling load by "60-70%"), not to accounting/capitalization adjustments (explicit management denial of the latter in response to an analyst question). Segment-level margin ranking (illustrative, per CBO): co-working > managed office > back-to-back, i.e. the segments management is prioritizing for growth (managed/back-to-back) carry structurally lower unit margins than co-working, a trade-off for scale and longer revenue-visibility.
capex / expansion (watch slippage): Fixed assets +161% YoY (Rs 35.25 cr) on workspace infrastructure/tech platform/managed-office expansion. New-centre cycle: ~3 months design-to-ready, then 3–6 months to reach stabilized occupancy from launch — watch for slippage against the "10 lakh sq ft operational by end-FY27" target given this lag; management itself flagged that not all upcoming area will show up in FY27 revenue (full benefit spills into FY28).
capital allocation: IPO proceeds (RHP-committed Rs 1.04 cr deployment plan) over-deployed to Rs 1.24 cr per management, funding sq-ft expansion from ~1.1–1.5 lakh sq ft at listing to ~7.5 lakh sq ft committed today. Incremental growth now also funded by debt — long-term borrowings increased materially during the year (finance-cost commentary — see §2 data-quality flag) — management characterized the debt cost as favourable versus equity cost and "within acceptable" limits, but did not give a target leverage ratio despite being asked directly.
risks & watch-items:
- **Data-quality/reporting-control flag:** management could not immediately explain a discrepancy in its own live segment-revenue slide during the call (see §2) — worth monitoring for a corrected investor deck and for the accuracy of segment-mix disclosures going forward.
- Small, single-country, largely single-region (NCR-concentrated) revenue base (~Rs 36 cr) — high operating and execution leverage to occupancy/ramp timing at new centres.
- Extended onboarding/ramp period (3–9 months per new centre) creates revenue-recognition lag versus committed area — FY27 guidance of "10 lakh sq ft operational" will only partially convert to FY27 revenue by management's own admission.
- Rising leverage/finance costs alongside aggressive capex-funded expansion; no firm leverage ceiling given.
- Commodity-like, low-differentiation industry per management's own framing ("without technology business does not exist... everyone is developing a dashboard") — no client names disclosed, so customer concentration/retention cannot be independently verified beyond management's qualitative assurance of low attrition.
- Pending Ind-AS conversion (targeted FY27) means FY26 reported margins are not on a comparable lease-accounting basis to larger listed peers — like-for-like comparison should wait for the converted numbers.
- Still an SME-platform listing (~1 year old); not yet resolvable in our own metadata universe (no ISIN/NSE mapping available at present).
management quality / tone: Candid rather than promotional on a couple of fronts — CEO voluntarily flagged and did not paper over the segment-slide numbering error live on the call, and MD/CEO explicitly declined to give a revenue number for FY27 rather than offer an unsubstantiated projection when directly pressed by an analyst ("Rohan"). Tone otherwise confident/aspirational on long-term ambitions (national player, "one of the biggest" in 3 years) without matching quantitative backing — treat forward qualitative claims with more caution than the quantified area/mix targets.
non-obvious takeaways:
- The strategic pivot from co-working to managed-office/back-to-back is explicitly margin-dilutive per unit (co-working > managed office > back-to-back in per-deal profit %, per CBO's own framing) — the growth thesis is a scale/volume trade against per-unit margin, not a margin-accretive mix shift; watch consolidated EBITDA margin closely as mix shifts further toward managed/back-to-back.
- Company is preparing to move to Ind-AS specifically because it believes its EV/EBITDA "pre-rent" (non-lease-accounted) numbers make it look cheaper than IFRS/Ind-AS-reporting larger peers — implying reported FY26 EBITDA is not on a like-for-like basis with sector peers today.
